Industry observers note that “Today we are announcing the arrest of 29-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht on a criminal complaint charging him with maliciously starting what became the Palisades Fire in January,” Bill Essayli, acting U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California, wrote via X on October 8, 2025.

“The complaint alleges that Rinderknecht started a fire in Pacific Palisades on Newly introduced Year’s Day — a blaze that eventually turned into one of the most destructive fires in Los Angeles history, causing death and widespread destruction.”.

According to recent reports, the Palisades Fire burned more than 23,000 acres of land in communities in and around Los Angeles, including Pacific Palisades, Malibu and the Santa Monica mountains. It was fully contained on January 31.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 has only just been released, so it might seem a bit early to start thinking about Grand Theft Auto 7. I swear I’m not just writing an “Everything we know about GTA 7” article just so I can stuff a post with the “Everything we know about GTA 7” keyword and have Polygon own “Everything we know about GTA 7” search queries. That would be quite a gambit.

Especially for a search term as competitive as “Everything we know about GTA 7.”.

Recent findings suggest that but the truth is there actually are some infinitesimal snippets of information already making the rounds about GTA 7. It can feel like grasping at straws; again, GTA 6 only just came out. But it’s never too early to start the “GTA 7 when???” conversation in the comments section of every Game Awards and State of Play YouTube stream. Here’s everyth– oh, you know the drill.

According to recent reports, the wait for GTA 6 has been atypically long — for the series, for its developer, and for video games on the whole. It’s been 13 years since GTA 5, eight years since Red Dead Redemption 2. Until now, Rockstar Games hadn’t even released a game for this console generation, which, if timelines for the PlayStation 6 and Xbox’s Project Helix are to be believed, will start winding down in a year or two.

In a recent development, in an interview ahead of GTA 6’s release, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson told Polygon that the studio’s map team started work as early as 2015. 2015! Remember how young we were? Remember how innocent we were? Remember how many fewer grays I had? Not that one? OK.

One of the reasons GTA 6’s development took so long was because, alongside making the game, Rockstar has also been refining the technology and processes needed to make games of this scale in the first place.

According to recent reports, “The engine, the tools, and the team we’ve built during this project will allow us to do things more swiftly,” GTA 6 co-head of development Phil Hooker told Bloomberg. “I feel confident that we can build on top of this and go more sideways than upwards to build more compelling content.”.

Recent findings suggest that “We foundationally changed a lot of stuff on this project,” added Rockstar North co-head Aaron Garbut during that same interview. “But now it’s done, and we’re not going to rip it apart.”.

There’s also the fact that Rockstar employs close to 5,000 people today, more than double it did around the end of development for Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018.

In a sprawling Guardian profile ahead of GTA 6’s release, Nelson suggested the series might eventually move beyond its signature satirical version of the United States, but that the studio still had its eye on America for the time being.

According to recent reports, “Never say never, but there’s still so much to do in America,” Nelson mentioned. “It doesn’t matter where you live … no one experiences the America that we’re portraying here in its fullness.”.

Previous Grand Theft Auto games have been set in major metropolitan areas like Los Angeles (Los Santos) and New York City (Liberty City). But even if Rockstar opts not to return to a previously seen location, there are plenty of cultural American hubs to satirize, including Chicago, Seattle, Boston, Washington, D.C., and New Orleans (a 19-century version of which appeared in Red Dead Redemption 2 as Saint Denis).

According to recent reports, let’s imagine Rockstar does leap straight from GTA 6 to a hypothetical GTA 7, as opposed to pivoting to long-desired sequels to either Red Dead Redemption 2 or Bully. We won’t hear about whatever the studio’s next game is for a long time, according to Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Rockstar parent firm Take-Two Interactive. He all but mentioned as much in an interview with TBPN (on Nov. 19, GTA 6’s release date, no less).

“We at Take-Two just went live with GTA 6 on Nov. 19. Wait, let me check my watch… Oh, it’s still Nov. 19,” Zelnick remarked. “I mean, guys, really? My father-in-law had a line about how whenever he had many great business achievements and a lot of admirers, and if he ever said anything nice, he’d say, ‘Oh, those are yesterday’s headlines.’ But it’s not even yesterday!”.

According to recent reports, before Rockstar even revealed a release date for GTA 6, fans of the series began riffing on GTA 7 in a dedicated subreddit. Yes, it’s intentionally tongue-in-cheek, with winking suggestions for its setting (Harrisburg, PA) and features (“will there be car?”), but it gets at the heart why such a thing can resonate in the modern internet in the first place: GTA 6 took a reallllllllllly long time. And as any Elder Millennial (or their therapists) will tell you, humor is a pretty effective coping mechanism.

According to recent reports, in fact, even GTA 6 has gotten in on the GTA 7 memes. Early in the game, as pointed out by some GTA fans on Reddit, you can see an in-game social media post quipping about the excruciating wait for a game called Race and Chase 7. The original name for Grand Theft Auto’s pitch, back in the ‘90s? Race ‘n’ Chase.

Looking for a genuinely cool tech gadget for less than $25? I’ve got just the one. The Casio WSB1000-1AV is a tough-built digital watch beaming with 1990s charm, but also a surprising smattering of modern tech niceties. Best of all, it’s 65% off for Black Friday.

According to recent reports, need an office Secret Santa/gift exchange option that won’t break the bank? Not sure what to get for your “cool” Gen Z cousin or technologically challenged parents? The answer is this deeply discounted $22 Casio watch, which, on pretty much any other day, would cost you $64. Here are five reasons why.

Marked down from $64 to just $22, this retro-1990s Casio digital watch features an onboard step counter and Bluetooth antenna for automatic time adjustments.

Hidden behind the screen of this seemingly ordinary digital watch is a Bluetooth antenna. Why would a dumb watch need Bluetooth? To pair it with your smartphone, of course. Once paired, the Casio WSB1000 automatically corrects the time based on your smartphone’s clock.

This means there’s no need to fuss with resetting the time when traveling across time zones. The bare-bones smartphone app can also be used to set or cancel an alarm on the watch, a timer, a stopwatch, and other basic functions.

Lastly, the onboard Bluetooth plays a key role in this next feature.

You’ll notice that the Casio WSB1000 has the words “Step Tracker” printed above the LCD. This refers to this little watch’s automatic step-counting feature. Who needs the best Apple Watch or the latest Fitbit?

Like an actual smartwatch or fitness tracker, users can set daily step-count targets. The WSB1000 not only tracks your total and displays it on the watch’s LCD, but it also demonstrates a dynamic graphic of your progress toward that day’s goal.

Bluetooth, meanwhile, is used to ping that step-count data back to your smartphone.

With onboard Bluetooth and automatic step-count tracking, battery life must be pretty short? Surprisingly, no. Casio notes that the common drugstore CR2016 battery in the watch should keep it powered for approximately two years.

Afterwards, a battery swap should be a relatively painless, affordable process, done either at home (if you're savvy) or at your local jewelry store.

While the Casio WSB1000 isn’t quite as durable as watches in the brand’s legendary G-Shock range, this digital wonder is rated for 100 meters of water resistance, the same as the latest Apple Watch Ultra 4. It also boasts a shock-resistant (though not shockproof), lightweight resin case.

Ultimately, for less than $25, you're not just getting a Bluetooth-capable digital watch with step counting; you're getting the Casio WSB1000, a 90s timepiece with a design that's Tom Cruise-running-atop-a-moving-train-cool; it's Keanu Reeves-stopping-a-speeding-bus-badass... etc.

And even if your intended recipient overlooks the step tracking and tosses this watch in a drawer for occasional use, when they do eventually pull it out and pop it on, you can be sure the time and date will be spot-on thanks to the Bluetooth connection.

Dan Bracaglia is the Tom’s Guide editorial lead for all things smartwatches, fitness trackers and outdoor gear. With 15 years of experience as a consumer technology journalist testing everything from Oura Rings to instant cameras, Dan is deeply passionate about helping readers save money and make informed purchasing decisions. In the past year alone, Dan has assessed major product releases from the likes of Apple, Garmin, Google, Samsung, Polar and many others.

An avid outdoor adventurer, Dan is based in the U.S. Pacific Northwest where he takes advantage of the beautiful surroundings every chance he gets. A lover of kayaking, hiking, swimming, biking, snowboarding and exploring, he also makes every effort to combine his day job with his passions. When not assessing the sleep tracking and heart rate accuracy of the latest tach gadgets, you can find him photographing Seattle’s vibrant underground music community.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there are a lot of characters in the wider "Hunger Games" universe, so I'll forgive you if you're only familiar with some of the bigger players like Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence), Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada in his origin film and Woody Harrelson in the original movies), Coriolanus Snow (Tom Blyth, Ralph Fiennes, and Donald Sutherland at various points throughout his life), Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson), or Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler). The latest installment in the literary and cinematic franchise, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," brings back some familiar faces and introduces latest ones too — so, who, exactly, is Proserpina Trinket?

Sources indicate that introduced in both the book and film version of "Sunrise on the Reaping," Proserpina Trinket is a bubbly, enthusiastic, and quick-thinking young stylist working to prepare Hunger Games tributes for all the Capitol-centric pomp and circumstance that takes place before the bloody Games themselves. (Yes, the teenage tributes get all dolled up before they're forced to fight to the death in a dangerous arena that's also trying to kill them. This world is sick!).

We don't know a ton about Prosperina besides the fact that she works with the extremely unreliable Magno Stift (Billy Porter), she's assigned to work on Zada's Haymitch alongside Vitus (Edvin Ryding), and her older sister is future District 12 chaperone and stylist Effie Trinket (played in this film by Elle Fanning and the original movies by Elizabeth Banks). What we definitely know is that she's played by Iris Apatow, a rising talent from a famous family who's shown up in a handful of TV reveals and several huge comedy movies from the 2000s.

It has been revealed that iris Apatow was born in 2002, and odds are you're familiar with her family. Her older sister, Maude Apatow, starred in "Euphoria" throughout its entire run. Her mother, Leslie Mann, is an acclaimed comedic actor. Then there's her dad Judd Apatow, a comedy kingmaker, producer, writer, and director who's helped make projects like "Superbad" and "Bridesmaids" and directed his own like "The 40-Year-Old Virgin," "Knocked Up," "Funny People," and "This is 40." Let's talk about those last three, because all of them feature the youngest Apatow. (The less stated about Judd Apatow's 2022 COVID movie "The Bubble," the better.).

Recent findings suggest that maude and Iris Apatow play Sadie and Charlotte, respectively, in both "Knocked Up" and "This is 40" — with their on-screen mother, Debbie, portrayed by Mann, and their father Pete by Paul Rudd as an Apatow stand-in. As for "Funny People," they also play Mann's daughters (in this one, Maude is Mable and Iris is Ingrid) with Mann as Laura, the ex-girlfriend of comedian and actor George Simmons (Adam Sandler), who's dealing with a life-changing health crisis. Sure, the Apatow daughters don't do a ton here, but they flesh out the universe in all three of their dad's films ... and it's notable that we watched Maude and Iris grow up on-screen, basically.

All things considered, Iris Apatow's career is just getting started. Still, over the past few years, she's dabbled in more adult fare (especially on the small screen), so it definitely seems like she's trying to show off her range.

Sources indicate that from 2016 to 2018, Apatow portrayed a supporting character, Arya Hopkins, who's tutored by series lead Gus (Paul Rust) on the Netflix TV show "Love," while on another Netflix exclusive, "Unstable," she appeared alongside Rob Lowe and his real-life son John Owen Love. The latter duo play tech CEO Ellis Dragon and his creatively inclined son Jackson, respectively, whereas Apatow plays Anna, an intern at Ellis' organization, itself aptly named Dragon, who also happens to be the former stepdaughter of the company's CFO Anna ("Fleabag" standout Sian Clifford).

Then there's "Tell Me Lies." A deliciously dramatic and dishy Hulu series created by Meaghan Oppenheimer, "Tell Me Lies" adapts (and improves) the book of the same name by Carola Lovering and ran for three seasons on Hulu. Apatow demonstrates up as a college student named Amanda in the third and final season, creating a problem for series regular Bree (Cat Missal) as she mentally and emotionally recovers from an affair with a professor named Oliver (Tom Ellis). After she finally gets out of Oliver's clutches, Bree notices that Amanda seems to be Oliver's next victim, sending her into a spiral.

You can see Apatow as Proserpina in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" in theaters now.

  • Prince William and Kate Middleton’s visit to India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony marked their first joint overseas tour in four years, and the couple used it as an opportunity to demonstrate their star power.
  • From Kate unexpectedly presenting an award and delivering a speech at the star-studded Earthshot Prize event to her and William playing cricket and traveling around Mumbai in an electric rickshaw, there have been plenty of photo opportunities and headlines around the world about the environmental initiative William is so passionate about.
  • Recent findings suggest that according to royals author Russell Myers, who followed the couple on tour, the speech Kate gave at the awards was kept top secret.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prince William and Kate Middleton’s visit to India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony marked their first joint overseas tour in four years, and the couple used it as an opportunity to demonstrate their star power. Through their action-packed itinerary, which took them from Mumbai to New Delhi, the Prince and Princess of Wales have paved the way for a new style of royal tour.

From Kate unexpectedly presenting an award and delivering a speech at the star-studded Earthshot Prize event to her and William playing cricket and traveling around Mumbai in an electric rickshaw, there have been plenty of photo opportunities and headlines around the world about the environmental initiative William is so passionate about.

Recent findings suggest that according to royals author Russell Myers, who followed the couple on tour, the speech Kate gave at the awards was kept top secret. “None of us knew she was presenting an award on the night, or that she was going to speak. The auditorium was packed. There were about 5,000 people there. It’s been the biggest Earthshot yet, and you could see Catherine was nervous, but she delivered an absolutely brilliant speech. I’d say her best yet.

In a recent development, “It’s been wonderful for her to be here, supporting William, and you can see they’ve really had fun. Because of ongoing terror threats, there have been less walkabouts, but it’s been a very successful and varied tour, and I think, being shorter than most tours, it sets a newly introduced blueprint when it comes to royal tours for the couple in the future.”.

Prince William and Princess Kate arrive to attend the Earthshot Prize awards night at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

There are seemingly already intends for another royal tour, states Myers.

Industry observers note that “William let slip that Australia is on the cards next, and if that’s the case, I imagine they will go as a family. They don’t want to be away from their children for too long, and what a way it would be to win support for the monarchy Down Under,” Myers says.

According to royals insiders, there had been some nervousness around the trip after the couple’s disastrous tour of the Caribbean in March 2022, when their visit was overshadowed by calls for the UK to apologize for slavery. Then some of their photo calls, including one that involved the couple riding in an open-top Land Rover, led to accusations of the royals appearing colonial and out of touch.

Industry observers note that “I think there has been a slight nervousness about how this tour would be received, but the reception has been really good,” Myers states. “The fact that William and Catherine have included a visit to Newly introduced Delhi to see Prime Minister Modi is a clever move. While this is a private trip to promote Earthshot, the Foreign Office was keen for William to meet with the Indian prime minister, so they have packed that into the itinerary too.”.

The visit to India has come at a time when the royals are on something of a charm offensive following a difficult year for the royal family, from Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor’s arrest to what one palace insider calls “the ongoing soap opera” with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has not been charged and has denied all allegations of wrongdoing.).

In a recent development, william and Kate are keen to carve out their own initiatives and projects focusing on their major priorities, including the environment, children’s early years, and mental health. With the challenge of having Harry and Meghan carrying out their own engagements, the Prince and Princess of Wales have been careful to establish clear parameters that set them apart as working royals. In one telling moment while on an engagement in Mumbai, Kate was asked for an autograph. She politely declined, so as not to breach protocol, a clear contrast to the Duchess of Sussex, who has signed autographs in the past.

“Catherine was asked to sign an autograph, but she was right not to. It wasn’t a snub; it was just adhering to protocol. An autograph could be sold for money,” notes Dickie Arbiter, former press secretary to Queen Elizabeth II.

According to recent reports, according to author Tom Bower, the royals are more relatable now than they were during the reign of Queen Elizabeth II, who famously never gave a press interview. In recent weeks, Prince William has appeared as a guest on The Graham Norton Show (to promote Earthshot), and he’s revealed how he drinks his cider and his love of wild swimming as part of his guest-editing stint for a recent concern of Country Life magazine.

Recent findings suggest that “The royals are more relatable, perhaps, than they ever have been, but they are not celebrities. There’s a danger of being too relatable, too much ‘one of the people,’ which means they can lose some of their mystery,” Bower says.

“William will have been advised to do TV appearances and take on media opportunities to bolster his public image. Of course, it’s charming to hear these nuggets and see this side of the prince, but I do think there’s a need to see and hear more from William about his broader aims. Over the years, Charles has made huge efforts to appeal to all cultural aspects of society. I’m not sure William has done that. He’s got to find a way of connecting with everyone, not just the younger generation,” Bower adds.

The Earthshot Prize awards have been a powerful way of demonstrating that William doesn’t just talk the talk; he is insisting on action.

Recent findings suggest that “The Earthshot is a master class in what needs to be done,” concludes Arbiter. “He’s pushing for environmental concerns and climate change, and he’s getting people to do something about it. The fact that he is so well supported, and by so many high-profile people, reveals his pulling power and influence.”.

  • Sources indicate that your router is a key piece of your home network, as it connects all of your other devices to the internet.
  • Your router's security protocol determines how encryption and authentication work to protect data that's transmitted over your network.
  • Some routers ship with factory default login credentials, which are the username and password you need to access your device's admin dashboard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that your router is a key piece of your home network, as it connects all of your other devices to the internet. This also makes it a highly valuable target for attackers and can leave your data vulnerable—especially if you simply plug your router in with its default settings unchanged. Whether your router is brand new or it's been a while since you audited your existing setup, these are the key settings to check and change right now.

Your router's security protocol determines how encryption and authentication work to protect data that's transmitted over your network. WPA3 Personal is the newest standard and the most secure, so if it's available on your router, enable it. It's compatible with devices that support Wi-Fi 6. Some older devices may not work with WPA3, in which case the WPA2/WPA3 Transitional mixed mode is a good alternative. At minimum, set your router to WPA2 Personal (AES).

Some routers ship with factory default login credentials, which are the username and password you need to access your device's admin dashboard. (This is not the same as your network name or wifi password, which you set up later.) Default router passwords are searchable online, which leaves your router's admin settings open to anyone. Once you get into your dashboard for the first time, change the default credentials and enable two-factor authentication for your admin account if available.

While some newer routers do have unique, device-specific defaults, it's a good idea to check this setting and ensure it's secure. If you're prompted to create custom admin credentials during the setup process, do it.

In a recent development, your network name, or SSID, is how your network appears when you search for available wifi. By default, this may be the name of the router brand or a short string of characters, but you should choose something unique to your network. Make sure there's no identifying personal information, such as your name or house number. While you may be tempted to hide your network and obscure your SSID, this may actually make your information less secure, so keep this setting disabled. You can, however, add "_nomap" to the end of your network name, which prevents your router's physical coordinates from being mapped by location databases.

The password to access your network should also be unique and secure and should not include obvious personal information. One option to keep it memorable and easy to type is to create a passphrase using five to seven unrelated words that, combined, have at least 16 characters.

Two additional settings that leave your network vulnerable are Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) and Universal Plug and Play (UPnP). The former lets users connect to your network with a PIN, which can be vulnerable to brute-force attacks. The latter allows smart devices to easily connect to your network—but this also allows malware to spread more readily. You may need to have UPnP on in order to connect devices initially but should disable it afterward.

Any easy win for your network security is segmenting traffic to different networks, so if one is compromised, the data on the others remain unaffected. Many wifi routers have a "guest mode," which creates a separate SSID and password that you can share with visitors instead of giving them your primary network credentials. You can also set up a separate network for all of your smart home and IoT devices so exploitable vulnerabilities in these devices don't put your computers, phones, and other connected devices at risk too.

In a recent development, routers run a type of software—called firmware—just like any other device. Firmware controls the router's core functions and is not immune to vulnerabilities, which can be exploited by bad actors. And, just like other types of software, manufacturers occasionally push updates to patch these flaws. Check your router's dashboard to see if automatic updates are toggled on. Some devices require an opt-in for auto updates during setup, so you should enable them if they are off. Some routers may even require manual updates—in this case, set a monthly or quarterly (at minimum) calendar reminder to check for patches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, ever since Tony premiered on the 2026 movie schedule, I’ve been looking forward to rewatching it with an HBO Max subscription. That’s because it’s such a lovely and unexpectedly heartwarming film about Anthony Bourdain’s cooking origins, and I found myself wanting to hang out in Provincetown again. However, while I did that, I also learned that the director Matt Johnson and star Dominic Sessa don’t exactly feel the same way about the film, as they described making it as “being stabbed in the stomach.”.

When CinemaBlend’s Hannah Saulic sat down to chat with the cast and director of the critically acclaimed Tony, she told them she loved the movie and described it as a “warm hug.” Matt Johnson went on to say he’s actually heard this sentiment from “so many people.” And Stavros Halkias, who plays Dimitri in the movie, noted that “it is sentimental.”.

I couldn’t agree more. The found family element of this film is honestly quite wholesome (despite the chaos). Along with that, hanging out with Tony as he figures out his life and falls in love with cooking is a really good time. Plus, there are parts of Tony that genuinely make me emotional. So, yes, in many ways, the movie is heartwarming, because he finds his people and his calling, and who wouldn’t want to spend time watching him do that?

However, making this movie was a totally different story. Making that point very clear, Dominic Sessa, who plays Tony, and Johnson, who directed it, had this to say:.

Industry observers note that well, I can’t say I blame Sessa, specifically, for having this reaction. I mean, the best gag in Tony is the one where he gets splashed in the face with water over and over again. He told us that filming those scenes “sucked,” and Johnson described Sessa’s experience with this gag as “a kind of prison torture.".

So, I can see why they’d also note that filming the movie didn’t feel like a hug, and in a way felt like getting “stabbed in the stomach.”.

However, again, that’s not how it reads on screen. As a movie, Tony is wonderful and not a torturous watch at all. To that point, Stavros Halkias jumped into the conversation to say:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Well, loukoumades are Greek donuts with honey, and they look delectable. And like Halkias pointed out, Tony is like a warm treat for viewers. Between Tony learning how to cook with Antonio Banderas’ Ciro, his realization that this is what he wanted to do with his life, and that Eric Ripert cameo at the end of the movie that comes with the first time Tony refers to himself as Anthony, it’s hard not to feel heartwarming energy radiating off this A24 flick.

However, when you rewatch it and feel that way, just make sure to remember and appreciate the fact that it was not that warm and cozy to make.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't.
  • Apple is presently beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure.
  • In a recent development, with the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't. But while most of us are running this version (or should install it as soon as possible), others are running something different—iOS 27.3.

Apple is presently beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure. With it, comes the return of the Health app, vertical Safari tabs, and Siri AI app actions, among other new features. But for consumers of Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, iOS 27.3 brings two rather notable changes—both of which are for the better.

In a recent development, with the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo. The foldable famously ships with Touch ID, the first latest iPhone since the third-gen iPhone SE to do so. While that isn't a problem per se, many of us are used to unlocking our iPhones with our faces. This update just lets new Duo owners keep up with that muscle memory.

Sources indicate that now, take note: This isn't Face ID. No software enhancement can introduce fresh hardware, so the iPhone Duo still doesn't have the camera tech required to power Apple's Face ID system. As such, the Duo's face unlock is likely not as secure as Face ID on other iPhones. Perhaps that's why your iPhone Duo will require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. This feature seems to be one of pure convenience: If you want to be able to unlock your Duo with your face (at least, some of the time), you can.

Recent findings suggest that what's more, this isn't a default setting. If you're running the beta, or if you're reading this after iOS 27.3 drops, you can find the option in Settings > Touch ID & Passcode.

Sources indicate that apple made a massive deal about the continuity involved with opening and closing the iPhone Duo. As you do, your content moves with you seamlessly—a very Apple thing to do. That remarked, you might expect folding the Duo to lock it, but it doesn't. You need to hit the side button to actually put the phone to sleep.

Sources indicate that iOS 27.3 changes that. If you so choose, you can enable a setting to lock your Duo whenever you close it. That won't work for everyone, of course—some users may still want to move between modes without worrying about locking their Duos. But for those who would rather lock their devices whenever they fold them up, the newly introduced option is under Settings > Display & Brightness.

It has been revealed that disney has produced many of the best animated movies of all time. They've been doing it longer than anyone else and, arguably, better than anyone else for decades. Unfortunately though, original animation has been a tough sell to audiences in recent years, and Disney's "Hexed" looks like it's going to suffer at the box office as a result of this trend.

Industry observers note that "Hexed" is at the moment eyeing an opening in the $23 million range, per Box Office Theory. That's across the full five-day, Wednesday to Sunday stretch since this movie is opening mid-week for the Thanksgiving holiday. The comedy "Focker In-Law" pits Ben Stiller against Ariana Grande and looks to win the weekend with around $36 million. For what it's worth, earlier tracking (via Deadline) had both movies doing between $40 and $50 million across the five-day stretch.

Industry observers note that more than A24's "Club Kid" or or the "Hershey" biopic, also releasing over Thanksgiving, it's "The Hunger Games" that will be a bigger glitch for Disney's latest. "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" will be a bigger hit than you realize, doing well over $100 million on opening weekend. That means, in its second frame, it could still easily take number one over Thanksgiving.

In a recent development, disney's latest centers on an impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie (Hailee Steinfeld) who discovers secret magical abilities which. Once unleashed, they hurtle her out of suburbia and into a vast witch realm called Hexe. Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand directed the movie, with Josie Trinidad co-directing.

It has been revealed that the big problem for "Hexed" is that these movies don't come cheap. We're looking at a budget of at least $150 million, if not much more. Even at $150 million, an opening under $30 million across a robust, long holiday weekend is close to a death sentence. Yes, there are overseas markets to account for and family-friendly movies can have long legs. Even so, the early estimates are rough, to put it kindly.

It has been revealed that it's especially disappointing because this feels like the right place on the calendar for the movie. "Moana 2" smashed box office records and led to the biggest Thanksgiving ever in 2024. That eventually became a $1 billion hit for Disney. But that was a sequel to a much-beloved move from the 2010s. Originals, from both Disney Animation and Pixar, have struggled mightily in the 2020s.

It has been revealed that case in point, "Strange World" bombed at the box office in 2022, taking in just $73 million worldwide. "Hexed" doesn't appear to be in such terrible shape but it's not looking good. Disney's "Wish" was also a big disappointment at the box office in 2023, doing $255 million worldwide. Decent for an original movie by today's standards but not nearly good enough to turn a profit.

The only thing Disney can hope for is that word of mouth amongst moviegoers is outstanding, which could give "Hexed" unusually long legs. Or that tracking is just wildly off and the movie actually comes in closer to earlier estimates. Either way, as it stands, this one looks like it just has one too many hurdles to clear.

Disney's "Hexed" hits theaters on November 25, 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • CD Projekt has confirmed that a physical version of The Witcher 4 will be released, even though the RPG is slated to launch after Sony Interactive Entertainment intends to stops producing physical games for PlayStation 5.
  • Sony aims to end the production of game discs for PlayStation consoles in January 2028.
  • "We’re massive fans of people having access to tangible collectible things.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt has confirmed that a physical version of The Witcher 4 will be released, even though the RPG is slated to launch after Sony Interactive Entertainment intends to stops producing physical games for PlayStation 5. Whether The Witcher 4 will be released on a physical disc is another matter entirely.

Sony aims to end the production of game discs for PlayStation consoles in January 2028. The Witcher 4 is the highest-profile AAA game currently slated to launch that year, and it comes from a studio that enjoys releasing its games physically. In an interview with The Game Business from August, CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski confirmed that CD Projekt would still like to release a physical version of The Witcher 4.

"We’re massive fans of people having access to tangible collectible things. We’re nerds ourselves, and we like that. We always supported that," Nowakowski explained. "So, whatever is the case, we’re going to be for sure having a box. We’re going to have a box that’s going to have some feelies in it. Something you’re going to be wanting to open up and enjoy.".

That stated, Nowakowski said he's unsure whether the game itself will be on a disc, as CD Projekt has no control over what Sony decides to manufacture. "We know what PlayStation has announced. And we have no influence on the policies of the first parties," he admitted. "The discs for the first parties, including PlayStation, have to be manufactured in their own factories. So, if they stop manufacturing indeed by 2028, then yes [we won’t have a disc].".

In a recent development, although Nowakowski went on to tell The Game Business that he has "no influence" over whether it'll even be possible to print discs for The Witcher 4, it's good that CD Projekt is committing to a physical release regardless. That said, it's clear that PlayStation needs to better explain its aims to developers, some of whom are clearly still expressing demand for physical discs.

Industry observers note that the Witcher 4 will be released on PS5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X sometime in 2028. Before then, fans of the series can look forward to a current-generation remaster of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt on Sept. 29 and the Songs of the Past expansion for that game sometime in 2027.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

The Saucony Endorphin Speed has been one of the most influential running shoes of recent years, setting the template for fast training sneakers that uses some of the materials and tech from top carbon plate racers.

With the line proving so successful, Saucony has been reluctant to change much about the shoe over the five generations to date, and even though the Endorphin Speed 6 is the biggest upgrade yet thanks to a new midsole foam, it mostly retains the same ride feel as past models.

It has been revealed that I’ve reviewed every model of the Endorphin Speed and I’ve always been a substantial fan. While that’s still true with the Speed 6, this category contains some of the best running shoes available, and there are some lighter, bouncier fast trainers I rate very highly, like the New Balance SC Rebel v1 and Dynafish Xiaonian.

According to recent reports, the Saucony Endorphin Speed 6 costs $180 in the U.S. and £180 in the U.K., which is a $5 price rise on the Endorphin Speed 5. It’s an expensive shoe, though not out of line with other plated trainers like the Hoka Mach X3 and New Balance SC Rebel v1.

Right now the Saucony Endorphin Speed 5 is widely reduced, dropping to $104 on Amazon in the Black Friday sales, which is a factor to consider when weighing up buying the Speed.

The Endorphin Speed 6 is at the moment available in five colors in the women’s shoe, and four colors in the men’s, including the white and yellow design I tested.

There is a wide version of the shoe available, though I found that the standard one fit me well in my normal running shoe size, the same size I’ve used with all past models of the shoe.

Saucony has added 2mm of foam to the midsole of the Endorphin Speed 6, which has a stack height of 38mm at the heel and 30mm at the forefoot, maintaining the 8mm drop of past models.

It weighs in at 8.5oz, which is 0.5oz lighter than the Endorphin Speed 5 in my size, a welcome drop for a speed-focused shoe.

The Endorphin Speed 6 has a simple mesh upper that has a little bit of padding around the tongue and collar, but mostly focuses on being lightweight and breathable.

It’s my preferred kind of upper on any shoe, since it’s not oppressively padded on the tongue or overly stiff around the heel, and I found the fit comfortable and secure throughout all my runs.

The Endorphin Speed 6’s main changes are in the midsole, which is made from a upcoming foam called PWRRUN PBX, which is meant to be lighter and bouncier than the PWRRUN PB that has been used on all past models of the shoe.

There’s also the higher stack and a redesigned nylon plate in the midsole, which aims to create a smoother, faster ride, with the Speedroll rocker on the shoe also contributing to this.

The changes to the midsole are noticeable on the run, though not as dramatically as I expected when looking at the spec sheet for the Speed 6.

Rubber is used sparingly on the bottom of the Speed 6 to keep the weight down, but patches cover the forefoot and heel of the shoe, and in my experience Saucony’s pelletized midsole foams are durable even when the foam is exposed on the bottom of a shoe.

Grip hasn’t always been a positive feature on the Speed line, but the Speed 6 provided me with reliable traction in wet conditions on both the road and the track during my testing.

After the very pleasant surprise of the original Endorphin Speed, which I ran over 300 miles in, I’ve found that the line has delivered a reliably similar experience with all of the models since.

There have been updates to make it more stable and comfortable, but ultimately all five versions of the Speed to date have had a smooth, fast and versatile ride feel.

This is still true of the Endorphin Speed 6 for me, and while that’s mostly a positive in that it performed well across a variety of runs in my testing, some might have hoped for a bigger change to challenge rivals like the SC Rebel v1 and cheaper, lighter options like the Adidas Adizero Evo SL and Dynafish Xiaonian.

I used the shoe for a couple of easy runs, two progression runs moving from easy to tempo pace, and a threshold track workout running 4 x 8min reps, and it felt great throughout.

I used the shoe for a couple of easy runs, two progression runs moving from easy to tempo pace, and a threshold track workout running 4 x 8min reps, and it felt great throughout.

The rockered midsole pushes you smoothly through your footstrike, and while the midsole foam isn’t as soft and springy as some, it does give a good amount of energy return off the toes.

I also found the Speed 6 to be quite stable and comfortable for easy runs, which is not always the case with plated trainers like this. I could happily use it for pretty much any kind of run, though it’s not as fast as a true carbon plate racer, or as comfortable as a max-cushioned cruiser.

To compare it directly to the Endorphin Speed 5 I did a short run wearing both shoes, and while the Speed 6 is a little bouncier and more comfortable, especially under the forefoot, I still felt the two shoes had a similar ride feel.

The Speed 6 is still a bit firmer than most super-trainers, and not as comfortable as more cushioned shoes under the toes. Some will like this more direct ride feel, but I appreciate the extra softness and bounce of a shoe like the SC Rebel v1.

Sources indicate that if you’re a long term fan of the Endorphin Speed line the Speed 6 will be a winner. It’s a mild improvement on the previous models with extra cushion and bounce, and delivers the versatile performance you expect from the line.

There is certainly a case for getting the Speed 5 instead in sales in my opinion, but the Speed 6 is a slightly better shoe overall and a successful enhancement.

The Speed line has been faced with increasingly fierce competition in recent years, and I don’t think the Speed 6 does much to change the equation on this front.

If you want a lighter, bouncier fast trainer, the Newly introduced Balance SC Rebel v1 would be my pick, while plate-free shoes like the Adidas Evo SL, Dyanfish Xiaonian and the new 361° Mega 3 Pro all offer fast, fun rides at a lower price.

As someone who would always have had the Endorphin Speed in my own rotation through the first few models, I’ve now moved on to shoes like this myself. Even though the Speed 6 is just as good as past models, I personally like the springier ride available in fast trainers.

  • In a recent development, borgo sits on one of those blocks in the high 20s that you swear you’ve never been down before.
  • On one occasion, my server was a painter who used to bartend at The Odeon, as painters have done for decades.
  • In a recent development, the twist is that my server’s art was also hanging on the walls of Borgo, as was his daughter’s art.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, borgo sits on one of those blocks in the high 20s that you swear you’ve never been down before. The restaurant opened in 2024 but feels like it’s been there forever, a place with a natural hum and not an ounce of perspiration. Its clientele is specific but unpredictable; when I went there this summer for lunch with a movie producer, we spotted a powerful name-brand media executive, an architectural bigwig who designs the homes of billionaires, and a two-time Academy Award–winning actor. A few nights later, I sat near Walter Isaacson, who’s a regular. And don’t just take it from Elon Musk’s biographer. Matthew Schneier, the chief restaurant critic at Fresh York magazine, recently named Borgo the city’s best all-around restaurant.

On one occasion, my server was a painter who used to bartend at The Odeon, as painters have done for decades. He met Ross Bleckner there, and David Salle. He used to have a massive loft studio in Williamsburg, but as rents went up, he moved deeper into Brooklyn, to Fort Greene, where he built a studio in his basement.

In a recent development, the twist is that my server’s art was also hanging on the walls of Borgo, as was his daughter’s art. That’s because he was Andrew Tarlow—the painter and restaurateur who kick-started the Brooklyn aesthetic with his restaurant Diner and, yes, also owns Borgo.

According to recent reports, after launching that instant hit in an old, reclaimed diner, Tarlow opened five more era-defining Brooklyn spots before finally venturing into Manhattan with Borgo. All along, he’s still been the artist who got a job at The Odeon so that he could meet his heroes. He’s still painting away in his brownstone, doodling on notepads during concept meetings. He’s had shows recently at galleries such as Tiwa Select; he’s loosely associated with the Galerie Sardine extended universe; and he’s someone whose work I’ve been told about for years by those in the know.

As they put it, Tarlow is an emerging artist who happens to own the best all-around restaurant in Manhattan, as well as a bunch of other successful spots in Brooklyn.

“I realized, opening Borgo, that I really loved working in restaurants—and not that I had forgotten, but I hadn’t actually worked services in a while until I opened,” Tarlow told me during a studio visit. “And then, in a similar way, I think—I love making paintings. I actually will paint forever, no matter what happens.”.

In a recent development, the studio had dozens of unstretched canvases heaped on the ground, some still rolled up, and others hanging via a pin on the studio wall. They demonstrated figures grappling with pain in fierce color-blocked fields, automatic-painting abstractions, faces fading into other faces. One painting was a portrait of the artist Joe Bradley, a friend.

The studio is in the basement of the Fort Greene brownstone where Tarlow has lived for two decades with his wife, Kate Huling, raising four kids in a kind of neo-boho paradise. There were no studio assistants, no art handlers, no frames, no boxes, no packaging—just the artist and the work.

“It was kind of just as chaotic as everything else there, but in the most perfect warm embrace of a way. I saw the pure energy that he put into his paintings and the stories that they told,” says Alex Tieghi-Walker, the founder of Tiwa Select, calling from London. “So many artists could be quite—rightfully so, but quite precious with their works. And I love that Andrew was just like, ‘Oh, pull out the ones you’re taking and just take them in an Uber home.’”.

Tarlow grabbed at a canvas bare-handed, one with a bit of a conceptual bent, and put it up on an easel.

“I’ve had this up on the wall for a while now, and I just continued to look at it because I’m happy with it. I’m also a little unsettled—I mean, I’m showing you the inside of my drawers. I’m also a little unsettled by how far it’s gone abstract-wise.”.

He told me he couldn’t really do his other job, the restaurant job, without painting at odd hours. They’re totally separate, but complementary in a cosmic way.

“What are the processes? Like you stated, for some people, it’s nine to five. Then you listen to the news, smoke a cigarette, drink coffee. It’s either working or it’s not. The door either opens or it’s not,” Tarlow said, gesturing around to his studio. “But I’m going to go here every day, and I’m going to push some paint on canvas.”.

It has been revealed that diner opened in 1999, a few years after Tarlow moved to the desolate southern tip of Broadway in Williamsburg—where the crumbling street dead-ends into the East River. While looking for a cheap studio space, he found a 6,000-square-foot loft across the street from an abandoned diner from the 1920s. The loft’s landlord bought the diner, and in 1999, Tarlow opened Diner with then partner Mark Firth—and watched as it was patronized by only the artists across the street.

“You could stand outside the restaurant in those days and not see a single person walk by,” he told Bon Appetit in 2010.

It has been revealed that tarlow kept expanding. He opened Marlow & Sons, and then the butcher shop and specialty food store Marlow & Daughters. He founded a bakery, She Wolf, and a literary magazine, Diner Journal. He operated the restaurant at the Wythe Hotel, but only for a few years. Instead of doing the easy thing, Vegas-ifying Diner in some fresh development on the Williamsburg waterfront, he got even weirder, opening a nautical bar called Achilles Heel in a far-out corner of Greenpoint.

According to recent reports, A dealer with a gallery in Tribeca was the first, but far from the last, to tell me I had to check out Tarlow’s paintings. After an introduction was brokered, Tarlow invited me to lunch at Borgo this past summer. The restaurant has many fantastic pork-laden dishes, but we ate almost entirely vegetables, as well as one very elegant, simple piece of fish. A summer lunch. We fell into an easy patter, talking about exhibitions, other artists—but mostly his painting practice. He’d been working on Long Island, not on the East End but in the middle. He’d had a few demonstrates. There was discussion of representation. He spoke about all this with an unpracticed earnestness and complete confidence. He sounded like a very prominent emerging artist, which, at 56, he is.

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t know if it’s just age or time, or I was too much of a young person, or a young mind, but I’ve been more secure with my ability to hold all these things in the same time,” he told me back in the studio. “I can go work tonight in the restaurant and feel perfectly confident in that work, and I can show you this work and feel perfectly confident in this work. Whereas, I think, as a young person, I felt like, Am I fake?”.

Sometimes it’s not the enfant terrible who breaks out—it’s the working parent, the person with a desk job, the successful entrepreneur who back-ends into revolutionary art making. Think William Carlos Williams writing “The Red Wheelbarrow” while working as a doctor in Rutherford, New Jersey. Or Ruth Asawa making art in her kitchen while raising six children in San Francisco. Or Jeff Koons working on Wall Street in order to earn money to make his sculptures. Having a demanding job actually granted them the freedom to be artists. Tarlow started drawing during restaurant concept meetings.

Sources indicate that sometimes Tarlow hangs his own paintings upstairs in his brownstone’s salon room, or at his house on Long Island, to see what they look like in the wild. The paintings have a confident thrust to them, with the colors bold-blocked in a way that reminds me of Albert Oehlen, drawing from Roman and Greek mythology in Twombly-esque riffs: visages multiplying and fading like a Kippenberger-ian pomo ride into the ether. Sure, any painter who’s spent time in Europe since the 1990s has wanted to be Martin Kippenberger. But Tarlow has an actual connection to him: Like Tarlow, Kippenberger was a lover of Italian food and good wine, and he made art to hang in restaurants. And like Tarlow, Kippenberger was a restaurant owner, balancing his studio practice with running Capri, a Venice, California, spot in which he invested after moving to Los Angeles in 1989. According to those present at the time, Kippenberger became a part-owner of the place because, as the artist put it, “You can’t get a decent Bolognese in Los Angeles.”.

As a bartender at The Odeon, Tarlow maintained a working painting studio but found it hard to produce art. After opening Diner, he skipped painting sessions in favor of opening businesses and starting a family. Once that duality settled, he started drawing on the move, carrying sketchbooks and working through potential paintings. Eventually, once the kids got old enough, he built out a studio in a nook of his 19th-century basement.

In a recent development, “I really started painting back downstairs. Let’s just say, after dinner, it was 8 p.m. and they were watching Nemo. No one actually needs me, they’re totally happy. My wife’s up there, everyone’s laughing, giggling with little fish,” he mentioned. “And I can just walk down here and do my thing. Having it in my house for sure is the only way I could do this amount of work, and for sure even get to this place. Because I do think you have to do a certain amount of work to get to this place unless you’re just a born prodigy. But when you think about the genius of Picasso or whomever, he made a million fucking paintings.”.

Tarlow didn’t really show anyone his work for a long time.

According to recent reports, “I met Andrew socially. I knew his restaurants way before I knew Andrew. And one day he was like, ‘Come and see my studio,’” Tieghi-Walker tells me. “It did not surprise me at all that he had an art studio in his basement and that these were the types of works he was creating.”.

It has been revealed that the show at Tiwa Select was on view right as Tarlow was getting ready to open Borgo. There was a certain amount of unconscious transference, Tarlow told me. For the Tiwa dinner, instead of creating name placards, the artist hand-sketched an artwork of each guest’s name on the paper tablecloth. Now, when a regular makes a reservation at Borgo, Tarlow will elegantly sketch out their name on the paper tablecloth.

It has been revealed that the showcasing of his art at Borgo marks the first time Tarlow has put his own work on the premises of his own restaurant. Tarlow doesn’t exactly promote this. When I asked about it, he told me that only one of his own works was up at the moment, then changed the subject. Alex Levy, the media strategist and theater producer, has been a regular at Borgo since it opened. “Borgo is the grown-up Platonic ideal of what a restaurant can be,” he remarked. After several visits, Levy, who also collects a bit of contemporary art, noticed what was on the walls.

“I complimented one of the paintings, and Andrew said, ‘It’s by my daughter.’ And then he pointed to another one and said, ‘That’s by me,’” Levy indicates. “I had no idea that there’s this whole other part of him.”.

Like Tarlow, Levy balances two seemingly divergent but strangely complementary careers—as a speechwriter on one hand, a Tony Award winner on the other—and Tarlow invited him to see his studio on Long Island. Levy bought a painting immediately. Seeing the studio, Levy claims, helped him realize, to some extent, what the special sauce is behind a place like Borgo. It’s for incredibly confident, hyperproductive creative types, run by an artist who has complete faith in his ability to work.

And for Tarlow, the focus and passion in one arena lead right into the passion for the other.

According to recent reports, “I’m also being very present for your needs in the same way as I’m trying to be very present with these paintings,” he stated. “They’re not separate boats. When the restaurant’s working, I feel creative inside of it.”.

According to recent reports, in July 2026, we got an enhancement on "Home Alone 3" (as we'll call it until further notice) that suggested Culkin's return was more likely than ever, as the actor reportedly paid a visit to the Disney lot where he met with studio head David Greenbaum. Now, in his What I'm Hearing newsletter over at Puck, Matthew Belloni reports that the 46-year-old actor will indeed appear in a latest "Home Alone" movie.

Sources indicate that according to Belloni, the "sequel/reboot" is "officially in development," with longtime writing partners Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg producing under their Point Grey banner. The report claims Rogen and Greenberg will finish up an original horror comedy project for Universal before working with Culkin on a script for the new "Home Alone" film. That's good news, as the duo couldn't be better suited to the material. (Disney, of course, has yet to officially confirm any of this.).

Ever since "Lost in Newly introduced York," the "Home Alone" franchise has delivered sequel after sequel that didn't need to happen — the most recent being the Mouse House's, to date, one and only attempt, following the Disney/Fox merger, to revitalize the saga with a sixth movie. But "Home Sweet Home Alone" once again failed to bring back Kevin McCallister. Now, however, things look set to change.

Recent findings suggest that in 2025, Macaulay Culkin embarked on a "Nostalgic Night With Macaulay Culkin" tour, during which he spoke about his surprisingly great-sounding idea for a "Home Alone 3" movie. Culkin's film would follow an adult Kevin McCallister who's become too focused on work at the expense of his young son. Kevin would then become locked out of his own house with his son still inside before having to break back in and avoid his son's ingenious traps in what is essentially a metaphor for working his way back into his son's heart. Not bad, right? For now, it remains unclear whether this is, in fact, the pitch Disney has greenlit, but it would make sense.

Sources indicate that culkin has seemingly been warming up to the property over the past couple of years. As mentioned, 2025 saw him launch the "Nostalgic Night" tour, during which he chatted positively about his previous two "Home Alone" movies. Then, in 2026, he played a grown-up Kevin in a McDonald's commercial. Now, pending official confirmation from Disney, it seems he'll return to the franchise proper, with Matt Belloni noting how the actor's two young sons likely played into his decision.

Belloni also highlighted the massive popularity of Culkin's first two films, which reliably shoot to the top of the most-watched streaming charts every holiday season. Per FlixPatrol, right on cue, the original "Home Alone" is back in the Disney+ movie charts, jumping from number seven on November 15, 2026, to number two as of the following day, where it sits at the time of writing. The other films in the saga? Nowhere to be seen. Lord knows the "Home Alone" movies need a major revitalization, and you couldn't do better than Culkin's return in that regard.

Sources indicate that the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is hitting a significant milestone this year and will be turning the major 100. To celebrate, they are pulling out all the stops, including adding favorites, both newly introduced and old. One returning balloon has fans emotional as the announcement comes after the tragic death of Fiona the Hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden. Now that Macy’s has brought back its blue hippo for the 100th parade, Fiona fans have a request.

The beloved hippo became a global sensation following her premature birth in January 2017, and after receiving round-the-clock care, she began to thrive. She was also the first Nile hippo to be imaged prenatally via ultrasound at the zoo and the first born there in 75 years. However, on November 19, she swallowed a knit hat that was accidentally tossed into her enclosure, and it tragically led to her premature death. The loss hit hard for a lot of fans. One Reddit thread suggests that Macy’s blue hippopotamus “should totally dedicate it to Fiona,” and it has fans responding with comments like:.

In addition to the balloon possibly representing Fiona, it also has a long, legendary history. It was first unveiled in 1931, and during that parade, they decided it was a good idea to release giant balloons into Fresh York City. You may be asking yourself, why? I’ll tell you. Each balloon had a price tag, and whoever found a balloon and returned it to the department store would receive that amount as a prize. The blue hippo balloon was never returned, and even after an offer of $100, nobody came forward, leaving the balloon lost to history.

To ring in the parade’s massive birthday, they’ve decided to bring back the blue hippo, but this time, it’ll keep its feet tethered to the ground. It will be joining an assortment of upcoming additions, including everything from KPop Demon Hunters to Bluey. There’s something for everyone in the family to enjoy, and if you weren’t already, this year’s celebration could make you become a parade person.

The new balloon is reportedly going to look like a more modern version of the 1931 balloon seen below:.

It has been revealed that if the blue hippo isn’t enough to sell you on the parade, then maybe some new floats might. We’ll be seeing a variety of newcomers, including "Hogwarts Holiday," which features a Harry Potter-themed float that will celebrate (and promote) the newly rebooted series on HBO kicking off in December. The cool floats and balloons are an opportunity for brands (like Starbucks) to promote themselves with whimsical, colorful, and unique floats or balloons.

Additionally, it will include Tom Jr., which is a latest turkey addition to the parade, and Tony Sarg’s Amazing Marionettes, which pays tribute to the original parade puppeteer. There is also a mix of performers to look forward to, including The Voice’s new favorite coach, Queen Latifah.

However, a lot of Fiona fans will be watching to catch sight of the blue hippo and are hopeful it will do her justice with a sweet tribute or at least a special place in the parade.

During an interview for The Morning Show in Canada, the star of The Odyssey (one of the biggest box office success stories on the 2026 movie schedule) explained how that sweet moment unfolding in front of him reminded him of all the moments he’d shared with his own daughter at Goofy’s Kitchen in the Disneyland Hotel. A post shared by Loryn Powell (@lorynpowell).

Industry observers note that when I first saw the video, I immediately thought, “Now there’s a dad who’s having a flashback of a memory with his own daughter.” So it warmed my heart to hear directly from the Good Will Hunting star that that’s exactly what happened. When we think of Matt Damon, we picture the international film star, the public friendship with Ben Affleck, or even the Damon/Kimmel faux feud that started back in the early 2000s. This is the November 20, 2026 edition of True Colors, a look inside the global deals and colorful critiques that make the art world go round, with a weekly guide to the must-see openings, auctions, and fairs.

It’s True Colors, from Fresh York, where over the course of a few days billions of dollars have been spent at auction houses. Nvidia has lost more than $2 trillion in market cap since early October, but on Thursday, Anthropic’s IPO minted a class of new billionaires. It’s whiplash. As one dazed art dealer mused aloud on Monday night in the elevator at Sotheby’s: “It seems like money’s lost all its value.” Maybe the money, but not the art. Amid a surreal era of wealth creation and artificial intelligence, once-in-a-century oil-on-canvas masterpieces only get more covetable. Two Van Goghs from the same collectors have now sold for $190 million apiece, both in the span of a year.

Recent findings suggest that one thing remains constant: Everybody has to eat dinner. And increasingly, they’re doing it at Borgo, perhaps the best all-around restaurant in New York—where the owner is a semisecret acclaimed painter. I talked to Andrew Tarlow about maintaining a practice as a serious, boundary-pushing painter while running a Manhattan restaurant.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of restaurateurs: Michael Chow opened his first Mr. Chow in London nearly 60 years ago, and the spot is still as good as ever. A few works from Chow’s collection, some made specifically for the restaurant, are on view at Gagosian on Madison Avenue. I recently spent some time with him (and, briefly, Larry Gagosian) going through works by Ed Ruscha, Julian Schnabel, Jean-Michel Basquiat, and Andy Warhol, as well as many portraits of Chow himself.

We’ve also got reports from the Baby2Baby Gala in LA, the Ballroom Marfa Gala in Harlem, and a special dinner in Tribeca. And all the gossip from the auctions.

Mentioned in this problem: William Acquavella, Steve Wynn, Steve Cohen, Patrick Drahi, Charles Stewart, Jackie Wachter, Anthony Haden-Guest, Leonardo DiCaprio, Vittoria Ceretti, Jeff Koons, Frances Outred, Andrew Tarlow, Walter Isaacson, Matthew Schneier, Ross Bleckner, David Salle, Valentina Akerman, Joe Bradley, Kate Huling, Alex Tieghi-Walker, Alex Levy, Albert Oehlen, Ignacio Mattos, Louis Shannon, Victoire Bourgois, Nate Lowman, Julian Schnabel, Dustin Yellin, Meredith Darrow, Annie Morris, Michael Chow, Lady Gaga, Jim Dine, and Larry Gagosian.

According to recent reports, van Gogh’s Châtaigniers en fleurs sold for $190.4 million, including fees, Wednesday night at Sotheby’s Breuer building headquarters on Madison. It’s the most expensive work sold at auction this year, and easily among the top 10 priciest things to ever be publicly auctioned. It’s a bit insane to say this, especially about a single canvas that sold for more than the total value of the art set to be on offer at Art Basel Miami Beach next month, but that price feels a bit like a…disappointment? The on-request estimate for the work was $180 million, and the hammer price fell well short of that, at $165 million. Bidding in the room was thin, and the lot was guaranteed by Sotheby’s. Though it’s unclear where the exact guarantee price landed, it was probably around the estimate.

According to recent reports, honestly, it’s a relief to the house and the seller—the family of the Argentinian collectors Carlos Pedro Blaquier and Nelly Arrieta de Blaquier—that this painting sold at all. A Jewish collector bought the work in 1909 from a Paris gallery. His heirs claimed, just days before the auction, that the work was later sold under duress due to Nazi persecution, entitling them to receive restitution. The parties came together over an eleventh hour deal, terms undisclosed, to allow the sale to go through.

According to recent reports, so who bought it? The winning bidder in the room was William Acquavella, the patriarch of one of New York’s great art-dealing families, who has an august gallery on the Upper East Side. It’s unclear for whom he bought it. In the past he’s been known to broker art deals on behalf of former Las Vegas casino tycoon Steve Wynn. In 2013, Acquavella was the winning bidder on a Francis Bacon tryptic for $142 million—that time on behalf of Wynn’s ex-wife, the late Elaine Wynn. (The piece is currently on view at LACMA, where Elaine Wynn was a co-chair of the board.) Steve Wynn has been more of a seller than a buyer recently, so the jury’s still out on whom Acquavella was on the phone with Wednesday.

In a recent development, the $190 million price tag is an almost exact match for the amount someone else paid for another Van Gogh from the Blaquier-Arrieta family. Reports say that, in 2025, Christie’s conducted a private sale where Le Zouave, a Van Gogh portrait of a soldier, sold for $190 million. While there’s no indication that the most recent buyer was someone connected to the AI gold rush, it’s surely indicative of the times that a Van Gogh has sold for 9 figures right around the moment that the seven cofounders of Anthropic have become worth about $20 billion—and around 600 Anthropic employees have become worth more than $100 million. When reached for comment through a rep, Acquavella didn’t get back to me.

— As I walked into Sotheby’s Monday for the first sales of the week, there were clients going downstairs to get their tables at Marcel, where diners can bid tableside while cocktails are served from a bar cart. Other clients went to a sumptuous overflow room with an open bar and a large spread of Marcel goodies. Those lucky enough to snag seats moseyed up to the sales room, where telecom billionaire Patrick Drahi, the owner of Sotheby’s, was standing in the back, near CEO Charles Stewart.

The 6 p.m. start time meant some collectors were still trickling in when Jackie Wachter snagged a Gerhard Richter work for a hammer price of $5 million. In the back of the room, white-jacketed waiters wheeled around with flutes of Champagne for those standing in the back. The writer Anthony Haden-Guest, a longtime Vanity Fair scribe whose book True Colors gave this column its name, walked in and took a seat in the back. One woman started taking selfies. As the contemporary sale got underway, Leonardo DiCaprio and his girlfriend, Vittoria Ceretti, walked down from the skybox and watched as an Agnes Martin hammered at $9.2 million. DiCaprio, a very serious collector, didn’t appear to be bidding, but no matter; he was still there at Sotheby’s. Auction week had officially begun.

— Over at Christie’s, the house sold a Georgia O’Keeffe that had been on view in an apartment in my neighborhood for more than 60 years. Suffice to say, there aren’t many expensive works of art that get discovered in apartments in the vicinity of Tompkins Square Park. I had to savor the lot’s beautifully poetic provenance, a phrasing that I don’t believe has ever been printed in an auction catalog previously: “Property from an East Village Private Collection.” It sold for $4.9 million.

According to recent reports, — The week’s hottest lot? Maybe a sculpture of a dog by Jeff Koons, Bob-Tail, that was first on view at the artist’s still-controversial “Made in Heaven” show. Estimated to sell for an ambitious high estimate of $3.5 million, it hammered at $9 million, or $9.7 million with fees. Former auction chairman Frances Outred remarked the sculpture was consigned by a college friend of his who bought it from Anthony d’Offay for a five-figure sum in 1995, “when the art market was in the doldrums and the Jeff Koons market was at its nadir.”.

— For a dinner on Tuesday, Galerie Sardine installed a long table where every seat had a great view of one of the Joe Bradley paintings that had been installed in a space on 9 White Street. It wasn’t exactly a tough sell to get the works at the dinner—Bradley is married to Galerie Sardine founder Valentina Akerman. The always exquisite Ignacio Mattos whipped up some Estela-level pinchos ahead of serving an unctuously rich rice-and-chicken dish.

— Ballroom Marfa held its annual gala Thursday at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine, which, as honoree Anne-Cecilie Engell Speyer reminded attendees, is the largest Gothic cathedral in the world. For context: The cathedral would take up nearly four whole blocks of downtown Marfa, Texas. In addition to Speyer, the honorees included photojournalist Lynsey Addario and musician Lyle Lovett, who was introduced by VF contributing photographer Mark Seliger. The evening raised $1.5 million for Ballroom Marfa.

According to recent reports, — After the auction on Wednesday, the gallery Entrance, a space opened by dealer Louis Shannon on Ludlow Street nearly a decade ago, hosted an opening for the painter Victoire Bourgois. Lots of artists were there to support her—Nate Lowman, Julian Schnabel, Dustin Yellin—and the event was followed by a dinner at the ultimate Dimes Square redoubt. That’s right: Dimes itself. Can you believe Dimes has been open for—checks age—more than 13 years? And guess what? After all the Dimes Square discourse, the actual restaurant itself still slaps.

It has been revealed that — The annual Baby2Baby Gala went down in LA last weekend. I wasn’t able to make it out West, but luckily for Vanity Fair, Tallulah Willis was on the scene and wrote a fabulous party report that you can read here. I also want to note that the live auction of artworks, curated, as always, by Darrow Contemporary founder Meredith Darrow, included an Annie Morris sculpture that achieved $410,000.

According to recent reports, on a Friday in November, I walk into Gagosian on Madison Avenue for a meeting with Michael Chow, the artist, collector, filmmaker, designer, actor, and founder of the restaurant Mr. Chow. There’s a portrait of Chow by Jean-Michel Basquiat, a portrait by Julian Schnabel, a portrait by Andy Warhol. There’s a drawing of Chow by David Hockney, made soon after Mr. Chow opened in London in 1968.

In a recent development, michael Chow: So I opened that restaurant. You’ve got Hockney, you’ve got fashion, you’ve got every single thing. It’s almost like a Dada movement on the First World War thing. This one is in London—all happening.

He starts talking about duopolys: Christie’s versus Sotheby’s, Coke versus Pepsi. There was an Italian restaurant in London’s Soho, so he opened a Chinese restaurant in Soho with Italian waiters. He has a theory about name-dropping.

Chow: I hate people who drop names, and Lady Gaga agrees with me.

True Colors: That’s a good one.

According to recent reports, why is name-dropping key? Because the minute I say “Napoleon,” you will go there immediately. So it saves a lot of time. Okay, so why am I saying that? Do you know who Robert Fraser is?

The art dealer from the ’60s. Groovy Bob.

I was looking forward to meeting him, blah, blah, blah. He was sitting there. Name-dropping. Sitting in front is Jim Dine. Name-dropping again. I say, “I would like to borrow some paintings.” I mentioned, “Just like”—do you know the Kronenhalle restaurant?

We walk over to the Hockney portrait of Michael Chow sitting in his restaurant.

Chow: The first person I went to is David. He drew one and I mentioned, “Boy.” You know what he did? Tore it all up.

Simultaneously, I went to Peter Blake. I say, “Give me a painting that’s the antithesis of racism,” which he did. At that time he’s into the circus, he’s into all that shit. All right? So I asked him, “Why did you do that?” He did a portrait. So now Peter Blake is fucking crazy. He loves the circus, he loves wrestling and all that shit.

Larry Gagosian walks in and gives Chow a fist bump. Gagosian takes a long look at the Schnabel and then flips through a book of drawings made by artists for 57th Street’s Mr. Chow when it was the art world’s clubhouse. We walk up to the Basquiat.

According to recent reports, true Colors: To have it as this sort of landscape, you have the horizon line here, but it’s almost like a Western. It’s almost cinematic.

Chow: Name me three classic Westerns.

It has been revealed that shane. The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance. High Noon.

According to recent reports, I’m going to act out the first scene of each. Okay, High Noon.

He uses his hand to pull a finger gun on me, then gets distracted by the Ed Ruscha and the Warhol double portrait.

Chow: Andy said, “Oh, what do you want?” I said, “Hold the color and add lots of diamonds.”.

Gagosian brings up Anselm Kiefer, and then Richard Serra.

Chow: If you look at the year 2000, Charlie Rose and Richard Serra, their conversation on the culture of China, and Richard Serra identifies very clearly what is fine art: poetry, music, sculpture, and painting.

Industry observers note that the works in the show are for sale. I ask Chow if he’s emotional about parting with them. He seems very calm.

Chow: I’m only a temporary steward of the works.

“Friends and Legends: The Collection of Michael Chow” is up at Gagosian’s 980 Madison space until December 22.

Apple TV's 10/10 Spy Thriller Just Made a Totally Ambitious Move
